title: Road Trip Arrival Time Calculator
description: Add a trip's driving duration to its departure time with the Road Trip Arrival Time Calculator — arrival clock time, stops made explicit. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, depart at 07:30 with 9 hours 45 minutes of driving ahead and the wheels stop at 17:15 — before the stops you honestly add.
quick_answer: The Road Trip Arrival Time Calculator adds a journey's travel duration to a departure date and time and returns the arrival time. Enter when you leave and how long the driving takes, and read when you arrive — the calculation every 'we'll be there by…' message should pass through first.

Hotels, ferries and hosts have clocks. Work backwards from theirs: latest arrival minus duration is the latest departure.
Durations over a day roll the date forward — the calculator handles the calendar so the itinerary cannot pretend day two is day one.

faq: What does this tool calculate?
An arrival date and time: departure + travel duration, with the calendar rolled correctly across midnight and days.
Do I need an account?
No. Two inputs, one arrival.
Can I rely on this for professional work?
For scheduling and promises, yes — as the arithmetic layer. Traffic and life remain outside it; pad accordingly.
Does the route include live traffic?
No. The duration you enter should be your realistic one; live traffic is a navigation layer, not clock arithmetic.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
It is why your duration is what it is. This calculator consumes the duration; the driving tools produce it.
Should stops be inside the duration?
Either include them in the duration you enter, or add them after — but only once. Double-counted stops make liars of us all.
What about time zones?
The addition is zone-naive: it works in the clock you think in. For cross-zone trips, do the addition in one zone, then convert the answer.
The trip crosses midnight twice.
The date rolls as many times as the duration demands — multi-day arrivals land on their true date.
Can I work backwards from an arrival?
Subtract the duration from the deadline: latest departure. The same arithmetic, run in reverse by you.
Daylight saving changes mid-trip?
Clocks are local and the calculator is zone-naive — adjust the result by the hour the destination gained or lost.
